chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
Affliction, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singles out the believer for, was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام,

so he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked, “Who among the people is most severely afflicted in the world?” He said, “The Prophets, then those most like them, then those most like them.” Then the believer is afflicted according to the measure of his faith and the excellence of his deeds. So whoever has sound faith and good deeds, his affliction becomes more intense; and whoever has feeble faith and weak deeds, his affliction is less.

key_terms.أَعْمَالِهِ: his deeds, especially their goodness and excellence
key_terms.إِيمَانِهِ: his faith, by whose measure the believer is tested
key_terms.النَّبِيُّونَ: the Prophets عليهم السلام, described here as the most severely tested
key_terms.الْبَلَاءُ: affliction, trial, or testing sent upon a person

ai.seo_question: Why do the Prophets and stronger believers face the most severe afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the severest worldly afflictions fall first upon the Prophets عليهم السلام, then upon those most similar to them in rank and virtue. It explains that a believer’s trials correspond to the strength of his iman and the goodness of his deeds, so greater spiritual worth is often accompanied by greater testing.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,
‘The afflictions were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws and what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Particularised the Momin with.

So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww was asked, ‘Who is the most severely afflicted of the people in the world?’ So hesaww said: ‘The Prophetsas, then the next most then thereafter those similar to the previous group and so forth’; and the Momin is afflicted in accordance to his Emān and the excellence of his deeds. So the one whose Emān is correct and his deeds are excellent, the more severe would be his afflictions, and the one whose Emān is light and his deeds are weak, would be with few afflictions’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“Once, trials and misfortunes and things that Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, has specially set for the believers were mentioned in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and the qualities of the believer.

The Imam said, ‘The Messenger of Allah was asked, ‘Who suffers the most in this world?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘The prophets suffer the most and thereafter people similar to them and then those similar in position to the second group and so forth. A believer suffers proportionate to his belief and good deeds; thus, whoever’ s belief is more correct as well as deeds their trails and suffering are more intense, and whoever’s belief comes from a weak power of reason and whose deeds are weak their trials and suffering are less intense.’”
